column4: I have always had a fascination with questions. Why is *something* true? What made it that way? How do we know? How are we sure? If *something* is true, what else is true? What is false? This fascination goes beyond a desire to be correct on a surface level, but to know deeply and precisely, and to be able to clearly articulate the new gained understanding.
column5: I have always been fascinated by questions. Why is *something* true? How did it become so? How do we know? How are we certain? If *something* is true then what else is true? What is false? This interest goes beyond a superficial desire to be correct؛ the aim is to know with depth and accuracy, and to be able to articulate the new understanding gained clearly.

column4: While communication is common, effective and precise communication is challenging. To effectively communicate a message the author and originator must have an idea. However, the idea alone like water on a hard surface-its edges and boundaries are poorly defined, fluid, and easily moved around.
column5: Although communication is common, effective and precise communication is difficult. To convey a message effectively, the writer and originator must have an idea. However, the mere idea, like water on a hard surface- its edges and boundaries are vaguely defined, fluid, and easily shift about.

column4: We use words, terms, and phrases to transform the raw idea from vaguely shaped to precisely shaped. Words give our idea a boundary, they help us distinguish and separate between what the idea is, and what it is not. Now our shaped idea must be transmitted and received through some medium. Whether in long form text, like this book, or short form text, like a social media post, or in oral form, like a conversation or a video recording, the medium transmits the now well-formed idea to the recipient.
column5: We use words, terms, and phrases to turn the raw idea from a vague form into a precise form. Words give boundaries to our idea؛ they help us distinguish and separate what the idea is, and what it is not. Now this molded idea must be sent and received through a medium. Whether in long written form, like this book, or in short written form, like a social media post, or in spoken form, like a conversation or a video recording, the medium delivers this well-formed idea to the recipient.

column4: So far, we’ve only discussed the originator and author of the idea. For an idea to be useful, the recipient must receive, decode, and understand the message accurately. The transmitted and received messages should align closely.
column5: Up to now we have only spoken of the originator and author of the idea. For an idea to be useful, it is necessary that the recipient correctly receive the message, decode it, and understand it properly. The messages sent and received should be closely aligned.

column4: Every great human work is the by-product of effective communication. One man’s labor can only accomplish so much. To really build or perform something great, many men (speaking here generically of mankind) must labor together in a shared purpose, with a shared idea. Barring naturally occurring disasters (like a volcanic eruption) we also know that the greatest calamities to ever occur usually did so in significant part because of missing, broken or distorted communication. Truly life and death are in the power of the tongue (Proverbs 18:21).
column5: Every great human achievement is the result of effective communication. The labor of one person can accomplish only to a limited extent. To truly build or accomplish something great, many people (speaking here generally for humanity) labor together with a shared purpose and a shared idea. Setting aside natural disasters (such as volcanic eruptions) we also know that the greatest catastrophes in history often occurred largely because communication was absent, fractured, or corrupted.
